title: First Canadian Place
status: Source authoring in progress; no visual, geographic or maximum-fidelity approval

references.evidence: Web-extracted PDF text, pages 1-3. Screenshot fetch timed out and local download returned HTTP 403; no visual review claimed.
facts: Page 2 gives average office slab-to-slab height 12 ft 8 in (3.8608 m), standard clear ceiling 9 ft (2.7432 m), and mullion spacing 10 ft (3.048 m).
Page 1 describes a 23 ft (7.0104 m) main entrance lobby ceiling and a three-level retail complex.
Page 3 lists office lift banks serving floors 3-23, 24-42, 43-56, and 57-72.
references.caution: Average office spacing does not establish every slab datum or the podium/plant levels. The 10 ft mullion statement does not independently establish the spandrel panel count or corner bay geometry.

references.role: Council on Vertical Urbanism (formerly CTBUH), building height registry
facts: Architectural height 298.1 m; tip height 355 m; highest occupied floor 287.1 m; 72 above-ground floors.
Height definitions use the lowest significant open-air pedestrian entrance as reference.
references.caution: Roof mast location, support geometry and the other aerial heights still require independent visual evidence. Do not use the mapped 292 m or a different secondary occupied-height value as a replacement for these separately defined datums.

imagesInspected.notes: Dusk exterior: horizontal white spandrels, dark recessed corner strip, high BMO identity panel and rooftop aerials.

Construction photograph: larger new spandrels above rig and small original marble pieces below. Wide new panels align with pairs of narrower vision lights. Do not model the temporary suspended rig as permanent building geometry.
Comparative montage includes an altered after image. Useful for design intent, not independent as-built roof/site evidence.

facts: Project dated 2012; 72 storeys.
White custom fritted glass replaced the original marble; the public retail podium was also renovated.
Reports 5,370 spandrel panels, which differs from the executive architect's count; do not derive the facade layout from this total alone.

references.role: Architect of record and design collaborator
facts: Completed 2012.
Over 5,600 white glass and bronze panels replaced 45,000 marble panels.
Re-entrant corners use tinted glass.

Page 30 compares old small marble joints with larger new spandrels. Page 31 identifies the triangular frit option selected. Page 33 shows flush broad panels, thinner retaining trims and the existing window band beneath.
Page 37 text reports 5,625 fritted panels and 80 panels per floor; retain the differing counts as source-specific quantities.
references.caution: Several illustrations are design alternatives or renderings. Do not treat them all as executed geometry.

facts: Level 27 is shown as a square-like plan with four re-entrant corners, a central core and regular perimeter column bays.
Published rentable area 29,185 square feet is not an exterior plan dimension. No dimensioned outline is visible in this sheet.

references.role: Halsall project presentation, Building Science symposium, July 30, 2012
facts: Page 43 shows the typical facade section, corner return and closure trims; its embedded dimension text is not legible at the inspected resolution.
Page 47 shows large prefabricated glass spandrel panels and layered glass construction.
Text identifies separate face/corner marble populations and retained window assemblies, so the model must distinguish cladding from vision glazing.
Text on PDF page 56 gives approximately 9 ft from structural slab to suspended ceiling, not the floor-to-floor height.
Interior tenant-door standards must not be used to infer the building's street entrances.
Two principal guyed lattice masts and a smaller central pole, multiple antenna/dish assemblies and a rooftop equipment enclosure are visible.
The crown has a wide white glass band with BMO identity panels.
references.caution: Photographic geometry is primary evidence. The page describes several station assignments as best guesses; those assignments and its conflicting roof height are not adopted.

facts: White triangular frit panels, narrow metallic joints, glossy wall panels, a deep colonnade, overhead rectangular light openings, granite skirting and cylindrical bollards are visible.
references.caution: Image is linked, not redistributed or used as a texture. Exact street-level layout and dimensions remain to be registered.

mapEvidence.caution: Existing cached OSM evidence; 292 m differs from the published roughly 298 m architectural height. The antenna/top datum needs separate evidence.

nextWork: Inspect current owner/architect photographs for lobby, podium and rooftop antennas.
Reconcile plan dimensions, facade bay count, and individual podium/plant/office datums using the owner's average office slab interval and the separate registry height datums.
Implement an original reusable triangular ceramic-frit material if the existing shared graph library cannot represent it.
Use separate corner returns, spandrel panels, vision windows, plant louvres and entrance members; do not treat the building as one white box.
Register the mapped outline and signed site orientation only after an independent reference fit.
